## The exam in one line
CRT on **Sun 1 Nov 2026**: 2 hours, 300 marks, pen and paper, Hindi + English. **Every wrong answer loses 1/3 of that question's marks.** Then an interview (CRT 75 : interview 25).

## How to use this app every day
1. Open **Roadmap**. Today's topics are at the top.
2. **Read** each topic (45–60 min). The reading is prepared the night before.
3. **Quiz** on it (15 questions, 20 min). Read every explanation, even for the ones you got right.
4. Do the day's **Mock** and finish the question target.
5. Stuck on something? Tap **Ask AI**: *"Explain why option C is wrong"*.

On a school day aim for **3 hours** (1 h morning + 2 h evening). On Saturday and Sunday aim for **6 hours**.

## Phase 1: Cover everything once (Sat 10 Oct to Tue 20 Oct)
Two topics a day: one *education* topic + one *general* topic. Daily 20 min of current affairs and 20 min of English/Hindi.

| Date | Education topic | General topic |
|---|---|---|
| Sat 10 Oct | Education policies (NEP 2020, NCF, NIPUN, PM SHRI, Samagra) | Reasoning: series, analogy, coding |
| Sun 11 Oct | RTE Act + child rights (POCSO, RPwD, JJ) | Quant: percentage, ratio, average |
| Mon 12 Oct | Pedagogy: learning theories (Piaget, Vygotsky, Bruner, Skinner) | English grammar |
| Tue 13 Oct | Pedagogy: intelligence, aptitude, individual differences, sociometry | Hindi व्याकरण (संधि, समास, मुहावरे) |
| Wed 14 Oct | Measurement & evaluation (Bloom, reliability, validity, statistics) | Static GK: Constitution + education articles |
| Thu 15 Oct | Office procedure (noting, drafting, dak, files, records) | Digital literacy |
| Fri 16 Oct | RTI Act 2005 | Current affairs Oct 2025 – Mar 2026 |
| Sat 17 Oct | CCS Leave Rules + LTC + joining time | Quant: SI/CI, profit-loss, time-work |
| Sun 18 Oct | CCS Conduct + CCA Rules, FR/pay fixation | Current affairs Apr – Aug 2026 + **first 50-question mock** |
| Mon 19 Oct | GFR 2017, GeM/procurement, school finance | Reasoning: blood relations, direction, syllogism |
| Tue 20 Oct | School management + Delhi School Education Act & Rules 1973 | Static GK: history, economy, culture |

## Phase 2: Mocks and weak areas (Wed 21 Oct to Tue 27 Oct)
- **Full 100-question mock** on Wed 21, Fri 23, Sun 25 and Tue 27 Oct, at **9:30 am** (the likely exam slot), timer on, in one sitting with a pen.
- On the days between: the **3 weakest topics** from the Progress tab (*Practise weakest* button), then a 25-question mock on them.
- Every evening: re-read *Last-minute facts* for 3 topics.
- Make a one-page sheet of numbers you keep forgetting (leave days, RTI time limits, RTE sections, PTR, dates of schemes).

## Phase 3: Sharpen, do not learn new things (Wed 28 Oct to Sat 31 Oct)
- Wed 28: last full mock + review.
- Thu 29 – Fri 30: only *Last-minute facts*, your one-page sheet, and 15-question mocks on weak topics.
- **Sat 31 Oct**: light revision only, admit card + photo ID + black ball-point pens ready, check the centre route, sleep by 10 pm.

## Exam day (Sun 1 Nov)
- Reach early. Read the instructions on the booklet and fill roll number and booklet series carefully on the OMR sheet.
- **Round 1** (about 60 min): answer everything you are sure of. Mark doubtful ones in the booklet.
- **Round 2** (about 40 min): doubtful questions (see the guessing rule below).
- **Last 15 min**: check the OMR bubbles match your answers. Never leave OMR filling for the end.

## The negative marking rule (important)
A wrong answer costs one-third of the marks a right answer earns.
- Sure of the answer → mark it.
- You can **rule out 2 options** → mark your best guess (on average you gain).
- You can rule out **1 option** → guessing still gains a little on average; guess if you have a reason to prefer one option.
- You **cannot rule out anything** → leave it blank (a pure guess gains nothing on average).

## Where marks usually slip
- Numbers in service rules and acts (leave days, time limits, sections). Revise them every 2–3 days.
- Statement questions: check **each** statement separately before choosing "1 and 2 only".
- Hindi and English questions are quick marks: do not skip the language section.
- Current affairs from **Jan to Aug 2026** matter most; the paper was most likely set by September.
